Q1_subagent_scoping.question: Sub-agents global across sessions, or per-session pools?
Q1_subagent_scoping.rationale: Sub-agents will gain long-lived per-session memory (planned feature). Isolation must be designed in from day one, not retrofitted. Templates and underlying model-client connection pools stay global; instantiated sub-agents and their memory live inside the session.

Q2_daemon_transport.question: TCP localhost or Unix domain socket?
Q2_daemon_transport.rationale: Default 127.0.0.1:PORT for safety. Config flag flips to 0.0.0.0:PORT for LAN/VPN access. Bearer-token auth becomes mandatory whenever bind address is non-localhost — daemon refuses to start with 0.0.0.0 and no token configured.

Q3_web_framework.question: Svelte+SvelteKit, React+Next.js, SolidJS, or HTMX?
Q3_web_framework.rationale: Smallest footprint (~10kb runtime), fastest iteration, native reactivity, no Redux/Zustand boilerplate.

Q4_backwards_compat_cutover.question: Auto-spawn daemon from --terminal, or require explicit --daemon &?
Q4_backwards_compat_cutover.rationale: Zero friction. Falls back to --standalone if auto-spawn fails or user explicitly opts out.

Q5_multi_attach_semantics.question: Multi-controller (any client sends inputs) or single-controller (first attacher owns inputs)?
Q5_multi_attach_semantics.rationale: Single human in the loop, single trading account. Input-collision risk is minimal and recoverable; lock-out cost of single-controller would hurt every day. Treat it like screen -x.

Q6_daemon_process_management.question: Auto-spawn only, systemd unit only, or both?
Q6_daemon_process_management.rationale: Auto-spawn for development and casual use; systemd unit at deploy/kaid.service for the homedevbox so the daemon survives reboots.

Q7_persistence_boundary.question: Client 100% stateless, or keep client-local prefs?
Q7_persistence_boundary.answer: client stateless for daemon-relevant state, local for pure display prefs
Q7_persistence_boundary.rationale: Anything affecting the agent or trading lives in the daemon. Pure display preferences (terminal theme, window geometry, web UI dark/light, keybindings) stay client-local.

Q8_scope_pace.question: Phased rollout or big-bang single cutover?
Q8_scope_pace.rationale: Each phase leaves current workflows working. Big-bang turns into a month-long branch.

components.name: kaid
owns: market data streams (Coinbase WS, kai-api polls)
persistent stores (watchlists, chat history, autotrade, ledger)

components.name: terminal client
components.responsibility: WS client + rendering + keyboard handling. Everything network/agent/NATS/market-data moves to daemon.

components.name: web UI client
components.responsibility: Same WS protocol as terminal client. Same events, same charts, same sub-agent updates. One protocol, two renderers.

sessions.definition: A named conversation context with its own agent runner, isolated state, and persisted UI/memory. Named so user can run multiple independent lines of work without stomping each other's chat history.
per_session_state: AgentRunner instance with LLM conversation state, tool budget, cancellation handle
UI state (chart_symbol, chart_timeframe, chart_source, chart_size_mode, chart_color_scheme)
sub-agent pool (instantiated from shared templates, per-session memory)

wire_protocol.rationale: Bidirectional, native browser support, native Python support, streaming-friendly, observable. NATS stays internal infrastructure for sub-agent dispatch and signal fan-out — not exposed to clients.
wire_protocol.multi_attach_semantics: All attached clients receive all events; any attached client can send inputs. Treat as screen -x.

scheduler.purpose: Daemon-resident scheduler that lets the user (or the agent on user's behalf) schedule prompts at a time, on a recurring schedule, or on an event. Triggered prompts run as normal turns inside a target session.
scheduler.why_in_daemon: Must survive client disconnects. A scheduler in the terminal would stop firing the moment user quits the TUI. Whole point is waking the daemon at 3am even with no client attached.

examples: first Friday of every month at noon UTC
time.implementation: APScheduler + croniter. LLM normalizes natural-language times into ISO timestamps or clean cron strings before calling the tool.

examples: if BTC drops 5% in an hour
when long-signal scanner publishes score above 0.8 for ETH
event.implementation: Predicate subscribers on the daemon's internal event bus (signals, market data, balance changes). Predicate is a structured filter object — no eval, no DSL parser.

execution_flow: Scheduler wakes (cron tick / event match / manual REST)
Look up owner_session by name; mark failed if missing
Construct input envelope with source=scheduler + job_id
Session processes as normal turn — agent runs, output streams, chat history gets [scheduled job: JOB_ID] marker
On completion: update last_run/next_run/run_count/last_result_preview, persist, emit scheduled_job_completed
If concurrency=skip and session busy, log + emit warning, don't enqueue
safety_rails: Tool budget cap per triggered run
Self-scheduling loop detection — same session + similar params requires user confirm
5-minute catch-up window for missed triggers on daemon boot (older misses logged + skipped)
out_of_scope: Not a workflow engine — no DAGs, no fan-out, no conditional-job-creates-job
No built-in email/SMS/Slack notifications (use the agent's existing tools instead)

web_ui.auth: Bearer token from workspaces/daemon-token.txt; mandatory for non-localhost binds

risks.risk: Protocol churn during Phase 2 invalidates Phase 6 web UI work
risks.mitigation: Freeze the protocol at the end of Phase 2; future additions are new message types only, never breaking changes

risks.risk: Daemon crash kills every attached session at once
risks.mitigation: --standalone stays available; auto-restart via systemd; persist session state on every input so a restart loses ≤1 turn

risks.risk: Race conditions between multi-attached clients sending conflicting inputs
risks.mitigation: Per-session input is a single asyncio.Queue; first input in wins; both clients see it in their token stream so UI stays consistent

risks.risk: Sub-agents share state across sessions and accidentally leak context
risks.mitigation: N/A — sub-agents are now per-session by design (Q1 decision)

risks.risk: Per-session sub-agent pools multiply RAM and model-client connections as sessions grow
risks.mitigation: Templates are shared; only conversation buffers and memory are duplicated. Underlying HTTP clients to local LLM / kai-api are pooled globally so sockets don't multiply with sessions

risks.risk: Per-session memory grows unbounded over weeks of use
risks.mitigation: Memory store enforces a per-session size cap with LRU eviction; user can /memory compact from a slash command

risks.risk: Self-scheduling loop: agent creates a job whose triggered run creates more jobs
risks.mitigation: Loop detection in schedule_* tools — same session + similar params requires user confirmation; per-session active-job soft cap; /schedule pause all kill switch

risks.risk: Daemon restart loses near-future scheduled triggers
risks.mitigation: 5-minute catch-up window on boot re-fires recent missed triggers; older misses logged + skipped to avoid wake-up flood

risks.risk: Triggered job runs while user is mid-conversation in the same session
risks.mitigation: concurrency: skip default for new jobs; explicit queue mode is opt-in. Either way the chat history clearly marks scheduler-sourced turns

risks.risk: Web UI maintenance burden competes with agent work
risks.mitigation: Keep web UI small — same protocol, ~5 components, TradingView handles the hardest piece

risks.risk: Backwards compat breaks existing workflows (--chat, --once, etc.)
risks.mitigation: All sub-commands stay in --standalone mode until explicitly ported; document which are daemon-native and which are not

risks.risk: Port conflicts on shared dev machines
risks.mitigation: Config default + env var override + fail-loud if bind fails

risks.risk: State sync drift between daemon's in-memory state and persisted JSON
risks.mitigation: Single-writer per session; every input triggers a persist on the session boundary; load-then-merge for state.json

what_does_not_change: Agent runtime — AgentRunner, LLM endpoint chain, tool dispatch, memory store, NATS internal bus
Existing 62 pytest tests must stay green through every phase
File locations the user already knows (workspaces/, agent-config.json, state.json, chat history JSONs)
Existing event bus stays as-is — scheduler is a new consumer, not a new data source
